newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 16.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
HIGH COURT PUTS BRAKES ON JANATA DAL PARTY ELECTION AGAIN

The Delhi high court on Sunday froze the June 7 decision to entrust the Janata Dal party presidential election to a retired judge of the Rajasthan High Court. This is the court's third order in a fortnight on the election. Bihar chief minister and Janata Dal's president Laloo Prasad Yadav described the order as a just direction. He said he had full faith in the judiciary and would abide by the court's order.
The Economic Times
FIXED DEPOSIT RATES SLUMP AS INVESTORS CHANGE PREFERENCE

Interest rates in the fixed deposit market are crashing again because depositors now prefer manufacturing companies to non-banking finance companies (NBFCs). Several NBFCs promoted by top firms and manufacturers are now offering 13 to 14 percent interest rates on three-year fixed deposits (FDs). Higher rates are now equated with higher risks.
DEMAND FOR CONSUMER GOODS FINANCE FALLS BY UP TO 30 PCT

The demand for consumer finance schemes dropped by 20 percent to 30 percent in the first half of the year. Countrywide Consumer Financial Services says sales are very poor this season. They targeted a growth of over 30 percent but it actually dropped. This is true for the entire industry, said the firm. Sources in the Kotak Mahindra Finance also said the number of finance schemes were falling every month.
RAMAIAH UPBEAT ON SUPPORT FOR SEVEN-YEAR QR PHASE-OUT

India will table a seven-year phase-out plan to remove quantitative restrictions on imports, Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaiah said. At the World Trade Organisation, India will be able to get the support of all developed countries for the new time frame, says the commerce minister. India cannot set a lower time frame. The ministry is likely to table the new proposal after getting cabinet approval which is expected within a week. India is also constantly in touch with all member countries of the WTO to get the proposal passed this time. Diplomats said this time the Indian delegation who will negotiate on June 30 will have more powers than that of the last time if needed.
Financial Express
INDIAN AIRLINES TO SELL BOEINGS AND TAKE THEM BACK ON LEASE

To ease cash flow problems, Indian Airlines will sell its fleet of 12 Boeing-737s and then get the same aircraft back on lease. The national carrier calculates that leasing the aircraft will prove to be less expensive than owning them. The airline plans to float a global tender to invite bids from international leasor companies for the contract. The firm will float a purchase and lease tender for these Boeing 737 aircraft. Leasing will reduce the airlines' overhead costs, said its director of engineering.
SEBI MAY QUEER RBI PITCH ON HLL PREFERENTIAL ISSUE PRICING

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) will submit to the Bombay High Court that its own guidelines on preferential allotment and not that of the Reserve Bank (RBI) apply to the title preferential allotment dispute involving Hindustan Lever (HLL), Ponds India and the RBI, a top SEBI source said. This may queer the pitch for the compromise formula submitted to the court last week by HLL and the RBI. The submission will be given when the consent order for a compromise comes up for hearing on Monday.
IDBI HALTS DISBURSALS TO CEMENT FIRMS

The Industrial Development Bank (IDBI) has put on hold all loan disbursements to the cement sector. The term-lending institution has taken this step due to a rapid build-up in the cement industry's capacity which led to a softening of prices. Oversupply in the market led to an intense price war between cement companies in the Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh states. There are, however, no greenfield projects pending with the IDBI.
Business Standard
FRENCH GOVERNMENT TO LOBBY TO CLINCH DEAL FOR AIRBUS

The French government will do everything it can to press Airbus' claim to the $3 billion medium capacity long range aircraft tender the Indian government has floated. Airbus is in competition with its main rival, Boeing of the United States, for the contract. The French transport minister will discuss the deal with the Indian civil aviation minister during the latter's visit to the Paris air show. Both Airbus and Boeing have roped in their national governments to bag the deal.
ITC BOARD CLEARS LICENSING DEAL FOR BAT PLC BRANDS

The Indian Tobacco Company (ITC) board has decided to opt for a licensing arrangement for the new foreign brands BAT Plc wants to introduce in India rather than a joint venture for them. The brands to be introduced in India include State Express 555 and Benson and Hedges. According to ITC sources, the Indian tobacco firm will manufacture and market the BAT brands under its own portfolio and pay a licence fee to BAT. The agreement is expected to be for 20 years to 30 years.
ITC TO PUMP TWO BLN RUPEES INTO ITC CLASSIC

The board of the Indian Tobacco Company (ITC) has decided to support its ailing financial services associate, ITC Classic. The board agreed to buy properties and land worth about two billion rupees from ITC Classic. ITC has also decided to back Classic for some more time, provided the Reserve Bank and other banks which had given loans to Classic agreed to the revival plan. The decision followed several weeks of deliberations and speculations about the fate of ITC Classic. According to ITC board sources, the arrangement is only for a short period and a strategic promoter or partner will have to be identified soon.
MEDIUM-TERM INSTITUTIONAL BORROWINGS MAY BE PRUNED

The Finance Ministry is examining a proposal to prune the size of medium-term external commercial borrowings (ECBs) of financial institutions and ask them to opt for ECBs of more than 10 years. The move follows fresh guidelines issued last week that freed commercial borrowings of over 10-year maturity from the annual cap of $8.5 billion. The step to free long-term borrowings signals the government's intention to scrap limits on external commercial borrowings. The ministry has already informed the financial institutions that their annual ECB clearance might be much less than requested.
IDBI NOT TO FUND MERGERS AND ACQUISITIONS

The Industrial Development Bank of India has decided not to fund acquisition and mergers of companies. Mergers and acquisitions as a corporate strategy came into the limelight with the merger of the Shipping Credit and Investment Corporation with its parent company. Several multinational companies merged in the last two financial years, both in the country and overseas.
The Observer
INDUSTRIAL GROWTH TO REMAIN UNDER 8.5 PCT IN 97/98

The Industry Ministry does not expect industrial growth to exceed 8.5 percent in 1997/98 (April-March), senior officials said, and blamed the Finance Ministry. The Industry Ministry did everything within its powers to lift controls and offer concessions to boost production, and the Finance Ministry should now do the rest, they said. They attributed the expected decline in the growth rate to a cut in public expenditure and a lack of credit available to a large section of industry.
BOURSE OPERATORS TO CASH IN ON NO-DELIVERY PERIOD

Bourse operators will have a field day from this week as a number of scrips are entering the no-delivery period. From the new settlement beginning Monday, scrips like Tata Power, IDBI, SBI, Mahindra & Mahindra, Tata Tea, Ingersoll-Rand, Andhra Valley and Tata Hydro are entering the no-delivery list. The market trend is controlled by foreign institutional investors, who have turned bullish in the medium- to long-run.
INFLATION EASES TO 5.93 PCT

The annual rate of inflation based on the wholesale price index (WPI) fell to 5.93 percent for the week ended May 31. It was six percent a week earlier. The inflation rate has been falling for the last four months and has shed more than two percentage points since February. The official WPI for all commodities (base 1981/82 100) remained the same during the week under review at 323.5 (provisional). The rate of inflation during the corresponding week of 1996 was 4.77 percent.
